findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed the following food to not be protected:
 - The chicken base container in the walk-in cooler (WIC) was not covered. CORRECTED - Person-in-charge (PIC) was informed and the container containing the chicken base was covered with lid. 
- A bag of onions to be sitting on the floor and not 6 inches above the ground. CORRECTED - PIC moved the bag of onions to a dry storage shelf.

Ensure foods are always covered and stored properly to prevent cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed wet cloth used for wiping surfaces to be on the counter. CORRECTED - PIC was informed and the wet cloth was transferred to the sanitizer bucket. Ensure wet cloths used for wiping equipment surfaces are kept in the sanitizer bucket when not in use.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the big chest freezer gasket to be torn. PIC was informed so as to get it fixed. Ensure food equipments are in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed the following non-food contact locations to have grease deposits and soil accumulations:
- The hood baffles have accumulation of grease deposit and soil accumulation. PIC mentioned he was waiting for the company cleaning the hood to render the service today, but at the time of the inspection the hood had not been cleaned and the company staff did not show up. The inspectors will spot check in 1 month to ensure the hood baffles have been cleaned properly to sight and touch.
- The shelve under the prep table across the fryers have accumulation of grease deposit.
- The microwave across the fryer have accumulation of food debris. PIC mentioned he had gotten a new microwave and would no longer be using the old microwave.
- The unused cooler across the triple sink has accumulation of dirt.

Ensure non-food contact surfaces are cleaned regularly so as to be free of grease and soil accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the floor under the fryer to have accumulation of grease. The PIC was informed and he mentioned he was waiting for the company to clean the hood before he cleans the accumulation of grease from the floor. Ensure the kitchen floor is cleaned as often as necessary.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed a box of raw chicken stored on top of raw beef in the walk-in cooler. The PIC moved the beef onto another shelf during the inspection. The walk-in cooler has a pallet designated for raw chicken storage. The inspector suggests posting a sign reminding all employees that chicken must always be stored on the pallet to avoid improper storage. Ensure that food is stored according to the proper storage order to protect food from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Observed personal milks stored on a top shelf above various customer foods in the walk-in cooler. The PIC moved the milk to the bottom shelf of the front triple cooler during the inspection. The inspector suggests placing a labeled container in the bottom shelf of a cooler designated for employee items. Ensure that personal items are always stored below and away from customer foods to avoid cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the sanitizer bucket was testing at 0 ppm (Cl) when the inspector arrived. After adding a capful of bleach the sanitizer bucket was testing at 150 ppm (Cl). The inspector reminded the PIC of the importance of testing sanitizing solutions on a regular basis and re-making them as needed. Ensure that sanitizing solutions always test between 50-200 ppm (Cl).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed the beach at the facility does not have an EPA registration. The inspector educated about the importance of using food grade bleach at the facility. The inspector will follow-up on 1/27/2025 to ensure that the facility has bleach with an EPA registration.
findings.citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed several foods stored in cardboard boxes or containers directly on the floor. The locations of food stored on the floor included the walk-in cooler, walk-in freezer, and underneath the front counter. The PIC stated they are in the process of purchasing more shelving and pallets. During the inspection some pallets for underneath the front counter arrived. Ensure that foods are always stored at least 6-inches above the floor to protect food from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed the single use utensils by the takeout window were stored with the handles and food contact surfaces intermixed. The PIC was educated about the importance of storing handles in the same direction to prevent contamination of food contact surfaces. During the inspection the utensils were moved into a different container to allow the handles to be stored vertically. Ensure that single-use utensils are always stored properly.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed construction has been done at the front service counter causing there to be a large amount of exposed wood. The PIC and inspector had a conversation about sealing (ex. paint) all the exposed wood to create smooth, easily cleanable surfaces. They were also reminded that any other bare wood exposed throughout the facility due to ongoing construction must also be sealed. Ensure that all surfaces remain smooth and easily cleanable. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Observed the following physical facilities need to be repaired: 

(1) The small holes throughout the facility, especially around the front hand washing sink, must be sealed.

(2) The edging piece that is coming off the wall to the right of the front hand washing sink must be re-attached to the wall. 

(3) The cove base to the left of the walk-in cooler, left of the walk-in freezer, and left of the back door must be repaired/replaced. 

(4) The triple sink must be sealed to the wall. 

Ensure that physical facilities are always maintained in good repair. Repeat violations from the pre-opening.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.
